```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

`qtl2mr` estimates selected-locus, founder-aware Mendelian-randomization
effects for qtl2-style multiparent data. In about five minutes, this walkthrough
loads a bundled fixture, prepares two loci, runs an analysis, reads its primary
estimate and warnings, and locates the shareable report.

The fixture is synthetic teaching and integration material only: it is not
independent method calibration, biological evidence, or application validation.

## Load the example

```{r load-example}
library(qtl2mr)
data("qtl2mr_example", package = "qtl2mr")
```

The fixture has 96 samples, eight founders, one chromosome, four markers, and
two selected teaching loci (`m1`, `m2`). Locus choice remains upstream in a
real analysis; `exposure_lod` is an illustrative label, not qtl2 calibration.

## Prepare the input

```{r prepare-input}
prepared <- as_qtl2mr_prepared_input(
  allele_probs = qtl2mr_example$allele_probs,
  pheno = qtl2mr_example$pheno,
  covar = qtl2mr_example$covar,
  kinship = qtl2mr_example$kinship,
  marker_map = qtl2mr_example$marker_map,
  selected_loci = qtl2mr_example$selected_loci,
  exposure = qtl2mr_example$exposure,
  outcome = qtl2mr_example$outcome,
  metadata = qtl2mr_example$metadata
)
stopifnot(validate_qtl2mr_input(prepared, require_selected_loci = TRUE))
```

## Run the two-locus quick start

```{r quick-analysis, results='hide'}
result_dir <- tempfile("qtl2mr-getting-started-")
result <- run_qtl2mr_analysis(
  prepared,
  adapter = "prepared",
  loci = 2,
  output_dir = result_dir,
  overwrite = TRUE,
  make_figures = FALSE,
  make_html = TRUE,
  verbose = FALSE,
  run_qtl2_validation = FALSE,
  run_heteroskedasticity = FALSE,
  diagnostic_bootstrap_B = 0L,
  heterogeneity_method = "chisq",
  run_loo_mr = FALSE,
  run_instrument_sensitivity = FALSE,
  progress = FALSE
)
```

Those switches keep this walkthrough fast by skipping optional diagnostics;
they are not universal analysis defaults. In particular, qtl2 parity validation
is deliberately not requested here. The primary LMM uses qtl2mr's internal
backend; the `qtl2` package is optional and is needed only for an explicitly
requested parity comparison.

## Read the result and warnings

```{r read-accessors, results='hide'}
primary <- qtl2mr_primary_result(result)
warnings <- qtl2mr_warnings(result)
```

```{r prepare-result-tables, include=FALSE}
primary_view <- data.frame(
  estimator = primary$reported_estimator,
  estimate = primary$theta_reported,
  `95% CI` = sprintf("[%.3f, %.3f]", primary$reported_ci_lower, primary$reported_ci_upper),
  numerically_bounded = primary$primary_reliable,
  row.names = NULL,
  check.names = FALSE
)

actionable_warnings <- warnings[warnings$shown_in_main_report %in% TRUE,
  c("warning_id", "severity"), drop = FALSE]
rownames(actionable_warnings) <- NULL
```

```{r read-result, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(primary_view, digits = 3)
knitr::kable(actionable_warnings)
```

The default `reported_estimator_policy = "diagnostic_only"` reports the
Star-space second-order estimate only for a numerically acceptable, bounded
fit. An unresolved or unbounded fit is left unreported; raw second-order and Two-step
diagnostics remain inspectable. This fixture commonly shows
`weak_block_first_stage`, a multi-founder heuristic rather than a
Stock-Yogo-calibrated failure rule.

The default estimate is in **SD of outcome per SD of exposure**. A bounded
fit does not guarantee 95% coverage: weak instruments, correlated loci and
same-sample selection remain limitations. `primary_reliable` is a legacy
name for this numerical check, not a claim of causal validity.

## Fit with a kinship matrix

The bundled fixture has no kinship. This second fit creates a nonzero
kinship from independent, synthetic background features. It demonstrates
the LMM input path, not a reconstruction of a real mouse pedigree or a
calibration experiment. Nothing is downloaded.

```{r kinship-example, results='hide'}
set.seed(401)
ids <- rownames(qtl2mr_example$pheno)
background <- matrix(rnorm(length(ids) * 24L), nrow = length(ids))
K <- tcrossprod(background) / ncol(background)
K <- (K / mean(diag(K)) + diag(length(ids))) / 2
dimnames(K) <- list(ids, ids)
prepared_lmm <- prepared
prepared_lmm$kinship <- list("1" = K)
prepared_lmm$hsq <- NULL  # estimate trait-specific hsq internally
lmm_dir <- tempfile("qtl2mr-lmm-")
lmm_result <- run_qtl2mr_analysis(
  prepared_lmm, output_dir = lmm_dir, make_figures = FALSE,
  verbose = FALSE, diagnostic_bootstrap_B = 0L,
  heterogeneity_method = "none", run_loo_mr = FALSE,
  run_instrument_sensitivity = FALSE, progress = FALSE
)
qtl2mr_primary_result(lmm_result)
```

## Open the useful files

Open the report interactively with
`browseURL(file.path(result_dir, "report.html"))`. The same folder contains
`summary.md` and `data/output_manifest.csv`. The knitted vignette cleans its
temporary directory; supply a named `output_dir` in your own analysis to keep
the results.

## Move to your own data

Use founder **allele** probabilities (sample x eight founders x marker),
numeric traits and covariates with sample IDs, an explicit selected-locus
list, and harmonized chromosome-specific LOCO kinship. The companion
`vignette("from-qtl2", package = "qtl2mr")` shows the upstream steps and
explains which choices are yours. A missing selected-locus list no longer
means "use every marker".

```{r cleanup, include=FALSE}
unlink(result_dir, recursive = TRUE, force = TRUE)
unlink(lmm_dir, recursive = TRUE, force = TRUE)
```
